result.summary: The landlord said "Please go ahead" (event 12) to sending a contractor to fit a new window handle, so the work is approved. I couldn't assign anyone because no contractor is named on the ticket, by the landlord or in the property's history. There's also a likely duplicate ticket (80) for the same job. I emailed the tenant to say the landlord has agreed, recorded the approval, and passed the ticket to the ops team to pick a contractor and check ticket 80. The ticket is on hold with a 2-day follow-up.

judgement.why_this_decision: The landlord's event 12 reply is a clear approval of event 9 ('May I send a contractor to fit a new handle?'), and classify_reply returned approve / auto. The normal next step is assign_contractor, but no contractor is named anywhere in the records up to 9 Feb 08:45, and I can't invent one. find_tickets also showed ticket 80 at the same address, with the same description, created at the same time. Sending a contractor from both tickets could mean two attendances. Picking a contractor and sorting out the duplicate are agency decisions, so I escalated at normal priority. The tenant got an update with a concrete next step.

alternatives_considered.why_not: No contractor is named on the ticket, by the landlord or in the property's job history, and inventing one isn't allowed. Ticket 80's later events (after 9 Feb 08:45) are future information, so I didn't use them to choose a contractor.
The landlord gave a clear go-ahead and asked nothing (event 11 asks whether a reply is needed). No reply is required.
Approval was already given clearly by email. Asking again would hold up the job for nothing.
The next step needs agency input (contractor choice, the duplicate). Without escalation nobody would pick it up.
